spec.raw_notes: Voice QoS for the front desk phones; 802.1X on exam room ports.
assumptions: user_count 90 = 58 full-time + 22 part-time techs + 10 visiting specialists; 6 remote billing staff excluded
Full redundancy (dual WAN + redundant core switches) from '24/7' and 'no single switch failure'
Kennel cameras, smart locks and the X-ray machine grouped into one IoT segment

checks.detail: All 6 subnets are valid and within RFC1918 private address space.
VLAN IDs [10, 20, 30, 99, 100, 110] are unique and avoid reserved IDs 1 and 1002-1005.
Every requested segment has its own VLAN (clinical, front-desk, guest, iot).
Room for all 90 users after reserving a gateway: staff 10.50.10.0/25 (125 hosts), guest 10.50.20.0/25 (125 hosts).
All 14 devices have a path to the WAN over 20 links.
Confirmed dual WAN (isp-a/router1, isp-b/router2) and 2 core switches with every access switch dual-homed and a 2-firewall pair reaching every core.
Guest VLAN 20 (10.50.20.0/25) is its own subnet and all WAN-bound traffic passes firewall1, firewall2 -- nothing bypasses it.
Evaluated GUEST-ISOLATION rule by rule on core1 Vlan20, core2 Vlan20: guest 10.50.20.0/25 is denied to all 5 internal subnets and 18 infrastructure addresses, and still reaches the internet.
All 6 VLANs have one gateway (HSRP virtual IP) that every core SVI, DHCP pool and managed device's default-gateway agrees on.
All 42 static addresses (including HSRP virtual IPs) are unique, and none of the 5 DHCP pools can lease one of them.
Traced the static routes hop by hop: core1, core2 reach the internet, and router1, router2 route and NAT all 6 VLANs, over every next hop including failover routes.
